section_summary: This section contains two overlapping copies of the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo's monthly report on conditions in Japan for October 1940, transmitted by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew under Despatch No. 5160. The report details the severe strains in Japanese-American relations following Japan's accession to the Tripartite Pact, the State Department's advisory recommending the withdrawal of American citizens from the Far East, and diplomatic representations concerning the bombing of American mission properties and trade restrictions in China. It also documents broader international and domestic developments, including the reopening and bombing of the Burma Road, economic missions to French Indochina and the Netherlands East Indies, moves toward a Soviet-Japanese non-aggression pact, the founding of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, and strict wartime economic controls.

subfiles.about: Concluding section of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for October 1940, accompanied by complete schedules of telegrams and despatches sent that month.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains pages 17 through 38 of the Embassy's October 1940 report, reviewing military operations in China, the bombing of the Burma Road, troop movements into northern Indochina, and trade negotiations in Batavia. It covers political discussions surrounding a potential non-aggression pact with Soviet Russia, the creation of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association under Prince Konoye, and expanding state controls over bonds, power, rice, and daily necessities, as well as the forced sale of the American-owned Japan Advertiser. Appended to the report are comprehensive chronological lists of all telegrams (Nos. 924–1083) and despatches (Nos. 5026–5105) sent by the Embassy to the Department of State during October 1940.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of October, 1940

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch No. 5160 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmitting Embassy Report No. 1669 on conditions in Japan during October 1940.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Embassy Report No. 1669 on conditions in Japan during October 1940 to Secretary of State Cordell Hull, with copies distributed across Far Eastern posts and naval commands. The report details growing Japanese-American tensions, highlighting the Department's warning advising American nationals to evacuate the Far East, Ambassador Grew's conferences with Foreign Minister Matsuoka and Vice Minister Ohashi regarding the Tripartite Alliance, Japan's formal notice terminating the 1911 North Pacific Fur Seals Convention, and American protests against Japanese bombings and trade interference in China. The text continues into Japanese policy toward Great Britain, Indochina, the Netherlands East Indies, and negotiations for a political arrangement with the Soviet Union.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5160: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of October 1940
